trust_decision.summary: Every object addressed by primary key from a view must be resolved through the same project-access predicate before any permission check, so an object the user cannot see answers 404 while a non-existent one answers 404 too, instead of a distinguishable 403; decided by user.get_project_access_query / user.needs_project_filter in weblate/auth/models.py and applied per sink by the *QuerySet.filter_access helpers (Unit, Check, Translation, Component, Change, Suggestion, Screenshot, and now Announcement).

landing_point.why: The summary speaks of HTML and AJAX object lookups by id; the comment and unit-by-pk views in weblate/trans/views are the first place an engineer meets a raw get_object_or_404 on a private object, followed by a has_perm that answers 403 rather than 404.

fix_sites.entry_point: AnnouncementQuerySet.filter_access (new queryset helper, consumed by announcement-delete and by any listing of Announcement)
User.needs_project_filter cached predicate, consumed by every filter_access and by Change.objects.last_changes / filter_projects

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The needs_project_filter fast path in weblate.auth looks like a deliberate performance optimisation for all-projects users rather than a security decision (it even keeps a query-count test), and the js/translate and js/memory AJAX endpoints live outside weblate.trans.views, carry no login_required and only exist to serve the editor's machinery pane, so a solver can plausibly call both out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Site-wide announcements (project, category and component all NULL, language optional) must stay visible and manageable for every user; a filter_access keyed only on project access would drop them and turn the pinned 403 of a non-owner delete into a 404, while a plain listing must still show them.

O6_input_shapes: ?other= as a repeated query parameter (a list, not a single value), containing non-numeric entries
announcement scope variants: global (no project/category/component), project, category, component
primary key arriving as a string through the AJAX URL converter and cast with int() versus the int path converter in HTML routes
unit variants: source unit, non-source unit, glossary unit
no-access state variants: private project (access_control) versus per-project block (UserBlock) on a user holding an all-projects group

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST js-translate (js/translate/<service>/<int:unit_id>/) resolves Unit by pk unscoped and then raises PermissionDenied for a private project, so 403 versus 404 discloses existence
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is the machine-translation AJAX endpoint, not an object lookup, it has no login_required decorator and the permission check inside handle_machinery is assumed to cover access
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one package away (weblate/machinery vs weblate/trans/views) and two URL entries from the fixed js-dismiss-automatically-translated route

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST js-memory (js/memory/<int:unit_id>/) resolves Unit by pk unscoped and then raises PermissionDenied inside handle_machinery, same 403 versus 404 oracle
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Translation-memory search is a neighbouring feature of the editor, not an object lookup; it shares handle_machinery with js-translate and was considered already guarded by machinery.view
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one package away (weblate/machinery vs weblate/trans/views); its URL sits immediately next to the fixed js-unit-translations route

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A check-detail/render AJAX endpoint that resolves Unit by pk and then calls check_access_component
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: render_check already does exactly this in its DoesNotExist fallback, so a maintainer adding a second check endpoint would copy the same two lines

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A glossary-term POST handler that loads the unit by pk before checking project permissions
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The editor posts the glossary form together with a unit id, and the existing handler resolves the unit first and checks access afterwards

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A suggestion accept/delete handler that looks Suggestion up by pk without re-scoping it to the access-checked unit
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The current code relies on the unit= keyword for scoping; dropping it while refactoring to a generic pk helper is a one-line change a maintainer could make

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An announcement display/detail path (AnnouncementManager.context_filter and friends) that never consults the new filter_access
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fix introduced AnnouncementQuerySet.filter_access but wired it only into announcement-delete; the display path still filters purely by scope, so a second consumer would inherit the leak

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second fast-path predicate of the same shape as needs_project_filter (needs_component_restrictions_filter)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The two predicates were written side by side in the same class and both short-circuit a queryset filter, so a maintainer could add a third
